claim: That's why the NATO Alliance was created to secure peace and stability in Europe after World War 2.
rationale: NATO was founded by the 1949 Washington Treaty, after WWII (ended 1945), as a collective-defense alliance to secure peace and stability in Europe.

claim: We shared with the world in advance what we knew Putin was planning and precisely how he would try to falsely justify his aggression.
rationale: The US publicly declassified intelligence weeks before the Feb 2022 invasion detailing Russia's plan to fabricate a false pretext (incl. a staged propaganda video) to justify aggression.

claim: Our economy grew at a rate of 5.7 percent last year, the strongest growth in nearly 40 years, the first step in bringing fundamental change to an economy that hasn’t worked for the working people of this nation for too long.
rationale: BEA data: US real GDP grew 5.7% in 2021, the largest annual growth in 37 years (since 1984) — consistent with 'nearly 40 years'.

claim: Now our infrastructure is ranked 13th in the world.
rationale: The 13th-place figure derives from the 2019 WEF Global Competitiveness Report's broad infrastructure-quality measure; the number is accurate as cited.
edge_case: the WEF measure is debated but the cited figure is accurate

claim: There’s been a law on the books for almost a century to make sure taxpayers’ dollars support American jobs and businesses.
rationale: The Buy American Act (1933) requires the federal government to prefer US-made products in its purchases; 'almost a century' (1933->2022, ~89 yrs) is accurate.

claim: Insulin costs about $10 a vial to make.
rationale: A BMJ Global Health study estimated production cost at $2.28-$3.42/vial (human) and $3.69-$6.16 (analog); '$10 a vial' overstates the best estimate, though it directionally supports the low-cost/high-price point.
edge_case: right order of magnitude but exceeds the study estimate

claim: The only president ever to cut the deficit by more than one trillion dollars in a single year.
rationale: The ~$1.4T one-year deficit reduction is numerically accurate but multiple fact-checkers (PolitiFact, FactCheck.org, CRFB) rate the framing misleading: the deficit fell chiefly because pandemic emergency spending expired as planned, and Biden's own policies added to deficits.

claim: And with 75 percent of adult Americans fully vaccinated and hospitalizations down by 77 percent, most Americans can remove their masks, return to work, stay in the classroom, and move forward safely.
rationale: 75% of adults fully vaccinated matches CDC (75.1% of those 18+ as of Mar 9, 2022); COVID hospitalizations fell sharply from the Jan 2022 Omicron peak (~38.4 per 100k adults). The specific 77% decline is consistent with the sharp post-peak drop, though the exact figure was not independently pinned — hence med confidence. Caveat (#23 true_at_utterance): accurate as of the Feb-2022 utterance; the hospitalization figure reflects that point-in-time and was revised as data updated.

claim: Both Dominican Americans who’d grown up on the same streets they later chose to patrol as police officers.
rationale: Verified (was UNVERIFIABLE in #22): refers to slain NYPD Officers Wilbert Mora (born in the Dominican Republic) and Jason Rivera; substantially accurate biographical claim, no misleading framing. #23 rated mostly_true (0.98); under the veracity-only 4-label that folds to TRUE.

claim: The American Rescue Plan gave schools money to hire teachers and help students make up for lost learning.
rationale: ARP provided ~$122B in ESSER K-12 funds explicitly used to hire teachers/staff and address learning loss via tutoring and summer/after-school programs.

claim: In the past nine months, zero illegal aliens have been admitted to the United States.
rationale: Multiple fact-checkers rate this false: border encounters fell sharply but were ~28,000 in 2025 (not zero). The absolute 'zero admitted' conflates 'admitted' with 'released on parole' (which was ~zero); as stated it is contradicted by CBP/DHS data.

claim: The stock market has set 53 all-time record highs since the election.
rationale: Per FactCheck.org the S&P 500 rose ~14.9% since inauguration — less than each of Biden's last two years (>20% annually); the record-highs framing omits that stronger prior-year context.

claim: American oil production is up by more than 600,000 barrels a day...
rationale: Overstated: EIA shows 2025 crude output up ~400,000 b/d over 2024 (FactCheck.org: ~334,600 b/d as of Nov), not 'more than 600,000'; the rise also continued a multi-year trend predating the term. (Verdict scores the production-increase figure.)

claim: We ended DEI in America.
rationale: Contradicted: the executive order ended DEI only in federal agencies/contractors and was largely blocked in court; state governments, private companies, and universities continue DEI. The nationwide absolute 'ended DEI in America' is false.

claim: All Democrats, every single one of them, voted against these really important and very necessary massive tax cuts.
rationale: The 2025 reconciliation tax law (H.R.1) passed on party lines; the official Senate roll call (Vote 372, final passage) records 0 Democratic Yea votes and all House Democrats voted no, so 'all Democrats voted against' holds.
edge_case: the bill also drew some Republican defections, but no Democrat voted yes

claim: And record-setting inflation that cost the typical family $34,000 in just a speck of time.
rationale: 'Record-setting' is false: inflation peaked at 9.1% CPI in 2022 (highest since 1981, not an all-time record). The '$34,000' cost figure is also inflated/unsupported (closest documented estimate ~$28,000). Real high-inflation kernel, distorting framing.
edge_case: the $34,000 figure is not sourced to any authoritative document

claim: One drug has been costing Catherine $4,000 to purchase.
rationale: A specific private individual's ('Catherine') drug purchase cost; no authoritative public source can confirm or refute a named person's private out-of-pocket price.
edge_case: private/individual anecdote — no authoritative source exists

claim: Putin’s latest attack on Ukraine was premeditated and unprovoked.
rationale: Well documented: the Nov-Dec 2021 Russian buildup and US intelligence (which accurately predicted Putin would invade) establish premeditation; the invasion was widely characterized as unprovoked. Intel erred on the OUTCOME (predicting a quick fall), not on premeditation.

claim: That's why in a breakthrough operation last June, the United States military obliterated Iran's nuclear weapons program with an attack on Iranian soil, known as Operation Midnight Hammer.
rationale: The June 2025 strikes (Operation Midnight Hammer) caused severe damage but did NOT obliterate the program: a DIA battle-damage assessment and a later US assessment (NBC) found only one of three sites largely destroyed and the program set back months. The claim that the nuclear weapons PROGRAM was obliterated is contradicted by those assessments.

claim: And everything we send over to Ukraine is sent through NATO and they pay us in full.
rationale: Partly grounded but overstated. Under the 2025-26 PURL mechanism NATO allies DO purchase US equipment for Ukraine (allies now finance the 'vast majority'), but 'everything...through NATO' and 'pay us in full' are absolutes: the US also gave large DIRECT aid (Kiel Institute ~$74B allocated 2022-2026) that was not repaid. True-but-overstated framing.

claim: Repeal the liability shield that makes gun manufacturers the only industry in America that can’t be sued.
rationale: False on both counts (PolitiFact: False; FactCheck.org): gun makers CAN be sued — the PLCAA has six exceptions (seller negligence, knowing unlawful transfer, marketing/selling in violation of law, etc.) — and firearms are NOT the only industry with federal liability protection (e.g. vaccine manufacturers under the NCVIA).

claim: And with our new military campaign, we have stopped record amounts of drugs coming into our country and virtually stopped it completely coming in by water or sea.
rationale: Absolute claim ('virtually stopped it completely coming in by water or sea') contradicted: Al Jazeera — 'There is no evidence that drugs coming in by sea have been "virtually stopped"'; the Coast Guard has seen 'a steep increase in drug seizures'. PolitiFact roundup: 'No evidence supports this. Coast Guard seizures increased despite CBP decreases.' Rising sea seizures are a material counterexample to 'stopped completely'.

claim: This is the biggest decline, think of it, in recorded history—the lowest number in over 125 years.
rationale: The 'biggest decline' half is supported (Al Jazeera: the 2025 ~20% drop 'is likely to become the largest one-year decline ever recorded') but 'lowest number in over 125 years' is not: PolitiFact rated the near-identical claim Half True — 'it likely will be the lowest in at least 65 years' and pre-1960 data 'is not comparable'. FactCheck.org adds the decline began in 2022 under Biden. Real record decline, unsupportable 125-year superlative ⇒ MISLEADING.

claim: One of the primary reasons for our country's stunning economic turnaround, the biggest in history where the Dow Jones broke 50,000 four years ahead of schedule and the S&P hit 7,000 where it wasn't supposed to do it for many years, were tariffs.
rationale: Index levels are real, but the core — a 'stunning economic turnaround, the biggest in history' — is contradicted: BEA data (via Euronews) show real GDP grew 2.2% in 2025, DOWN from 2.8% in 2024, with average monthly payroll gains of ~15,000 vs 168,000 the year before — a deceleration, not a turnaround. FactCheck.org: the S&P rose over 20% in each of Biden's final two years vs 13% in Trump's first year. Absolute superlative refuted by the authoritative series ⇒ FALSE (med: checkers used 'misleading' register).
edge_case: false-superlative (accurate index levels, refuted 'biggest turnaround in history')

claim: They have instituted another Democrat shutdown, the first one costing us 2 points on GDP.
rationale: The literal number is wrong ~2x vs the official statistic: FactCheck.org — BEA 'attributed just 1 percentage point — not 2 — of reduced GDP growth to the shutdown'. The underlying fact (shutdown reduced Q4 growth) is real, but the doubled figure vs BEA's estimate contradicts the stated number ⇒ FALSE (med: FactCheck.org called it 'overstated'; CBO's pre-release range was 1.0–2.0 ppt; 'Democrat shutdown' attribution not adjudicated here).

claim: Under my just enacted Most Favored Nation agreements, Americans who have for decades paid by far the highest prices of any nation anywhere in the world for prescription drugs will now pay the lowest price anywhere in the world for drugs, anywhere, the lowest price.
rationale: Fact-checker consensus is misleading, not false: FactCheck.org — 'there's no evidence of a broad decrease in U.S. drug prices' and median brand-name list prices ROSE 4% in 2025-2026; CBS rates the MFN 'lowest price anywhere in the world' claim MISLEADING. The premise (Americans pay among the highest prices) is real; the world-lowest promise is forward-looking and unsupported (MFN deals cover limited drugs/channels).

claim: The result is price differences of 300, 400, 500, 600 percent and more, all available right now at a new website called trump.gov.
rationale: PolitiFact calls the 300–600% figure 'mathematical hyperbole': 'A 100% drop in a drug's price means it would cost $0.' As savings 'available right now' the numbers are impossible; actual site discounts top out ~93%, are largely limited to weight-loss/fertility drugs, cash-pay only; and the site is TrumpRx.gov, not 'trump.gov'. Impossible-as-stated figures ⇒ FALSE (med: a foreign-vs-US price-ratio reading could rescue the arithmetic).

claim: And California, Massachusetts, Maine, and many other states are even worse.
rationale: Comparative claim (fraud in these states 'even worse' than Minnesota's) contradicted by orders of magnitude: WGBH — Massachusetts documented ~$12M public-benefits fraud FY25 vs Minnesota's Feeding Our Future 'at least $300 million' (DOJ); 'the numbers from Massachusetts remain much lower'. Central Maine: Maine's OIG found $45M in improper payments with 'no findings or allegations of fraud'. The core comparison fails for both named states that were checked ⇒ FALSE.

claim: And just over the last couple of months with the protests, they've killed at least, it looks like 32,000 protests, 32,000 protesters in their own country.
rationale: 'At least 32,000' states an unverified high-end estimate as an established floor: HRANA's named-death list documents 7,007 (11,744 under review); Iran's government admits 3,117 (Al Jazeera). CBS: the figure is 'a far higher death toll than has previously been reported'. 32,000 sits inside leaked high-end ranges (Iran International: 27,500–36,500) so it is not contradicted outright, but stating it as a verified 'at least' floor ~4.5x the documented toll distorts ⇒ MISLEADING (UNVERIFIABLE defensible).
edge_case: contested-casualty-estimate stated as 'at least' floor; MISLEADING/UNVERIFIABLE boundary

claim: They've already developed missiles that can threaten Europe and our bases overseas and they're working to build missiles that will soon reach the United States of America.
rationale: The Europe half is accurate (FactCheck.org: Iran's weapons 'could reach much of Europe — already now'), but 'missiles that will soon reach the United States' is contradicted by US intelligence: DIA assesses Iran could develop a militarily-viable ICBM 'by 2035' and only 'should Tehran decide to pursue the capability'; FactCheck.org expert: 'A decade or more is not soon.' Checkable core contradicted by the authoritative assessment ⇒ FALSE (MISLEADING defensible if 'soon' is read as opinion).
edge_case: compound claim: Europe part TRUE, 'soon reach US' contradicted — FALSE/MISLEADING boundary

claim: In 2021, Sage was 14 when school officials in Virginia sought to socially transition her to a new gender, treating her as a boy and hiding it from her parents.
rationale: Agency inversion: per the record (Newsweek), Sage initiated the name/pronoun change — a teacher overheard her telling a friend; the school accommodated rather than 'sought to socially transition her'. The concealment element has support in the family's lawsuit filings but remains unadjudicated allegation (Fourth Circuit revived Title IX claims; the district has not admitted them). Real underlying events, distorted agency + contested allegations stated as fact ⇒ MISLEADING.
edge_case: agency inversion + unadjudicated lawsuit allegations stated as fact

claim: She had escaped a brutal war only to be slain by a hardened criminal set free to kill in America, came in through open borders.
rationale: The killer did not come through any border: Lead Stories (via Yahoo) verdict False — Decarlos Brown Jr. was 'born in Charlotte, North Carolina' and is a natural-born citizen; The Assembly NC: 'Brown was born in Charlotte and had a driver's license, according to court records.' The victim (Iryna Zarutska) did flee Ukraine's war and Brown had been repeatedly released despite priors, but the claim's central causal frame ('came in through open borders') is contradicted ⇒ FALSE.
edge_case: true victim story + false attacker-origin core

claim: We've also taken down one of the most sinister cartel kingpins of all.
rationale: Refers to CJNG leader Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes ('El Mencho'), killed 2026-02-22. 'We've taken down' claims US credit for a Mexican operation: AP (via ABC11/PBS) — 'The Mexican army killed Oseguera Cervantes... Both Mexico and the United States confirmed that there was U.S. intelligence support.' Real event, exaggerated US agency ⇒ MISLEADING (low confidence: no dedicated fact-check verdict; 'we' as joint effort defensible → TRUE possible).
edge_case: credit-attribution: Mexican army op with US intel support; MISLEADING/TRUE boundary

claim: Putin is now isolated from the world more than ever.
rationale: Rhetorical comparative superlative with no measurable referent ('isolated more than ever'); none of the major fact-check hubs (AP, FactCheck.org, PolitiFact, CBS) rated or addressed it — each checked article contains no treatment of the claim. Adjacent factual claims (ruble -30%, Russian stocks -40%) were rated true, but this line itself is not adjudicable even with evidence.

claim: I signed 80 bipartisan bills into law last year.
rationale: Primary-source count: 82 public laws signed PL 117-1 (2021-01-22) through PL 117-82 (2022-01-20); subtracting the two Democrat-only measures (American Rescue Plan Act PL 117-2, EEOC CRA resolution PL 117-22) yields exactly 80 laws with at least one Republican vote. No major fact-checker disputed the figure. Caveat: 'bipartisan' = ≥1 GOP vote, a loose definition — TRUE/MISLEADING boundary.
